column1: Compassus Home Health - Capacity & Scheduling Concept Dictionary
Master glossary of every concept, variable, and definition that shapes home health capacity and scheduling. The Variable Inventory and Functional Scorecard tabs draw from this list.

column3: The total clinical visit work a branch's workforce can deliver over a period, by discipline and by service area, netted against work already committed - the supply ceiling and the open room left in it. Measured in productivity points (or visits) per clinician per day and week, rolled up to branch. A quantity-and-location question: how much can this branch absorb, for which disciplines, in which territories, this week.

The assignment of specific ordered visits to specific clinicians on specific days, and increasingly specific sequences and times, subject to discipline, availability, geography, and patient constraints. An allocation-and-matching question at the single-visit grain: who sees whom, which day, in what order.

Capacity sets the envelope and scheduling fills it. The same underlying data - clinicians, disciplines, territory, availability, visit weights, PTO - is capacity when read as totals and scheduling when read as assignments.

The communication and confirmation work that turns a schedule into delivered care and keeps the board stable - day-before confirmations, reminders, reschedules, coverage on call-outs, care-team updates. It both protects capacity (fewer failed visits) and consumes it (coordination time), so it is called out as its own band that ties the two together.
Reference code. SH = shared spine, C = capacity, S = scheduling.
Which side of the seam the factor sits on - Shared, Capacity, Scheduling, or Coordination (the execution layer). Color-banded down the sheet.
The grouping within a layer (Roster, Geography, Routing, Clinician pattern, Caregiver, Clinical timing, Compliance, Distribution, ...).
The specific capacity or scheduling factor being defined.
Why it matters and how it behaves in practice.

Hard = must be honored or the visit fails (patient refuses mornings; caregiver-present teaching).  Soft = optimize toward, break under pressure (clinician prefers an 8am start).  Structural = a fixed property of supply/geography.  Event = a demand trigger. Derived = computed live. Config = a policy-set constant.

How safely automation can act on the factor without unintended harm to the process, patient, clinician, or branch: High / Medium / Low. Composited from five factors - Legibility (captured in data, or informal knowledge?), Volatility (stable, or easily thrown off by a small error?), Coupling (isolated, or entangled?), Reversibility (recoverable, or lasting harm?), and Harm surface (who is exposed - patient, clinician, or branch?).

The setting implied by the confidence. Control = the system can decide and execute (High). Assist = the system proposes and a person confirms (Medium). Read = the system surfaces information only and a person owns the decision (Low).
Plain-language reason for the confidence and posture on that row.
Optional deeper systems view. Hidden by default - unhide the column for the fuller perspective; keep hidden for team and employer views.
Originating system(s) for the data: HCHB, Workday, Routing, Census, Manual, Config, Derived, or Telephony.
